assessment.nobel_worthiness: A foundational, wide-ranging political-economy contribution connecting institutions, electoral incentives, state capacity and fiscal policy to economic outcomes.
assessment.attribution: The three proposed laureates are central architects of the modern theoretical and empirical political-economy programme.
assessment.maturity: The work has been extensively developed, applied and integrated across political economy over several decades.
uncertainties: The broad programme has many important contributors, making a three-person attribution necessarily selective.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Population-scale administrative-data research has transformed measurement and understanding of intergenerational mobility and place-based opportunity.
assessment.attribution: Chetty, Hendren and Friedman are closely identified with the central mobility-data and estimation programme.
assessment.maturity: Its methods and findings have generated extensive follow-on work and have endured substantial policy and scholarly scrutiny.
uncertainties: The interpretation of mobility patterns and the relative importance of proposed mechanisms remain contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The reconstruction of long-run income and wealth distributions has reshaped research and public understanding of inequality, taxation and wealth concentration.
assessment.attribution: Piketty and Saez are central to the long-run distributional evidence, with Zucman central to offshore-wealth measurement.
assessment.maturity: The research agenda is mature, internationally influential and supported by large continuing data infrastructure.
uncertainties: Measurement choices, especially for wealth and offshore assets, remain consequential and debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The misallocation framework provided a powerful quantitative account of productivity differences and the potential costs of distorted resource allocation.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh, Restuccia and Klenow made the defining linked theoretical and quantitative contributions.
assessment.maturity: The framework has become a standard benchmark in development, growth and firm-level research.
uncertainties: Measured wedges can reflect forces other than policy distortions, limiting simple welfare interpretation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their models made political incentives and organized interests central to the economic analysis of trade policy.
assessment.attribution: Grossman and Helpman are the unmistakable principal contributors to this coherent research programme.
assessment.maturity: The work is longstanding, canonical and remains a central reference for political-economy analyses of protection.
uncertainties: The empirical portability of stylized lobbying mechanisms varies across political systems.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Partial identification fundamentally changed how economists draw credible conclusions when data cannot support point identification.
assessment.attribution: Manski is the decisive intellectual originator; later work broadened and operationalized the approach.
assessment.maturity: The contribution is deeply established across econometrics and applied research.
uncertainties: The candidate grouping combines foundational ideas with later methodological extensions whose attribution is more diffuse.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their work supplied enduring economic frameworks for exhaustible resources, natural capital and sustainability across generations.
assessment.attribution: Dasgupta and Heal are central early contributors to the programme represented here.
assessment.maturity: The work is longstanding and has acquired greater importance through subsequent environmental-economic research.
uncertainties: The appropriate valuation and aggregation of biodiversity and inclusive wealth remain scientifically and ethically difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This body of work established the lasting economic importance of early-life health and environments for later human-capital outcomes.
assessment.attribution: Currie, Almond and Cunha each made distinctive and influential contributions to the linked early-life and skill-formation agenda.
assessment.maturity: The evidence base is substantial and has generated broad research and policy influence.
uncertainties: Causal estimates and the scalability of interventions can depend strongly on setting and measurement.
